data.title: FluoGuide Enters Collaboration with Leica Microsystems, a World Leading Medical Technology Company
data.description:
KØBENHAVN, DK / ACCESS Newswire / October 2, 2026 / FluoGuide A/S (STO:FLUO) FluoGuide A/S ("FluoGuide" or the "Company"), a biotech company specializing in precision cancer surgery, announces a collaboration with Leica, a world leading medical technology company.

FluoGuide aims to improve outcomes for patients with cancer by enabling more precise oncology surgery. Our lead product, FG001, has been clinically proven to light up cancer and guide surgeons in performing more precise surgeries. FG001 has received both Fast Track and Orphan Drug Designations from the FDA, supporting the development of FG001 in high-grade glioma (HGG) in the US.

This collaboration agreement is a milestone in the development within brain tumor surgery where the aim is to optimize the usage of imaging systems and FG001 to enable better treatment for patients with high-grade glioma cancer. The focus of the current agreement is to support the clinical phase and to gather a body of evidence on Leica's technology platform.

The agreement has no initial payment and is non-exclusive. The terms of this agreement are not disclosed, and the agreement will not have an impact on the Company's financial results in 2026.

"We're pleased to join forces with Leica, a world leader in medical technology, to advance precision surgery for brain tumors. Combining FG001 with Leica's microscope systems aims to strengthen surgical accuracy and help improve outcomes for cancer patients," says Morten Albrechtsen, CEO of FluoGuide.

This information is information that FluoGuide A/S is obliged to make public pursuant to the EU Market Abuse Regulation. The information was submitted for publication, through the agency of the contact persons set out above, at 2026-10-02 18:25 CEST.

For further information, please contact:
Morten Albrechtsen, CEO
FluoGuide A/S
Phone: +45 24 25 62 66
E-mail: ma@fluoguide.com

Certified Adviser:
Svensk Kapitalmarknadsgranskning AB
Website: www.skmg.se

About Leica
Leica Microsystems, a Danaher company, supports the generation of insight from complex imaging data, enabling faster, informed decisions across life science, medical, and industrial applications. Guided by its purpose to reveal what is invisible, the company partners closely with customers to translate this insight into meaningful outcomes and contribute to a better and healthier world. The Leica Microsystems portfolio spans workflows from sample preparation to AI-enabled analysis. It builds on more than 175 years of expertise in microscopy, combining customer focus, continuous improvement, and innovation. As part of the Danaher ecosystem, Leica Microsystems connects imaging with complementary technologies and expertise to address broader scientific and clinical needs. Headquartered in Wetzlar, Germany, the company operates six major manufacturing and development sites and serves customers in more than 100 countries. Explore more at: https://www.leica-microsystems.com.

About FluoGuide
FluoGuide lights up cancer to maximize surgical outcomes in oncology. FluoGuide's lead product, FG001, is designed to improve surgical precision by lighting up cancer intraoperatively. The improved precision has a dual benefit - it reduces both the frequency of local recurrence post-surgery and lessens surgical sequelae. Ultimately, the improved precision enhances the likelihood of complete cure and lower healthcare costs. FluoGuide has demonstrated that FG001 is both effective and well tolerated. FluoGuide has entered partnerships with leading MedTech companies with the aim of accelerating development and commercialization. FluoGuide is listed on Nasdaq First North Sweden under the ticker "FLUO".

For more information on FG001 or FluoGuide's uPAR technology platform, please visit our home page www.fluoguide.com

data.title: Klick Health Named MM+M Market Access Gold Agency of the Year
data.description:
Klick Health Named MM+M Market Access Gold Agency of the Year

World’s largest independent health agency also wins nine client campaign awards across product launch, customer experience marketing, media, social media, health equity and social awareness, point-of-care marketing, and other categories

Klick Health took center stage throughout the evening at last night’s Medical Marketing + Media (MM+M) Awards, receiving the Market Access Gold Agency of the Year title plus nine campaign accolades, including five Gold trophies for “867-5309” (Cancer Support Community), “Project Inchstone” (Nestlé Compleat), and “MODDEN 26” (The Derek Sheely Foundation).

The agency’s Chief Medical Officer Holly Henry, PhD said, “This recognition is a testament to what happens when scientific rigor, deep access expertise and creativity work hand in hand, and you do work that truly matters to people. We are so grateful to our clients and to our growing market access and medical teams, who are hands-down the best when it comes to deeply understanding how to overcome the hurdles to patient access and adoption.”

Henry said the win was especially meaningful given the agency’s growing market access and medical communications focus, with Oxford PharmaGenesis recently becoming part of the Klick Health family to offer clients accelerated commercial success through broadened medical affairs and communications, market access, and RWE/HEOR offerings.

Klick’s client work was also recognized for excellence in healthcare marketing, including five honors (three Golds and two Silvers) for “867-5309,” the campaign it created for Cancer Support Community's and Gilda's Club's by turning a pop culture earworm into a lifeline for cancer support. The number, made famous by Tommy Tutone's classic tune, pairs with area code 272 (or CSC) to connect callers to the organization's free national Helpline. Activated across radio, streaming, PR, and social, the campaign generated billions of earned media impressions and increased Helpline calls by 216 percent in just one week.

Lisa E. Ireland, Executive Vice President, External Relations at Cancer Support Community, said, “These awards reflect the bold, creative thinking and genuine purpose that Klick Health brings to its work. Klick showed up as a true mission partner, united by our belief that community is stronger than cancer, and brought extraordinary creativity, strategic expertise, and commitment to help turn an iconic number into a memorable connection point for people impacted by cancer.”

Klick Health President Ari Schaefer added, “We’re extremely proud of how our teams collaborate with our clients to drive business results and make a difference in patients’ lives. Huge thanks to all our Klicksters who bring their curiosity and passion to developing outstanding work, and to our clients who trust us to help grow their brands and deliver lasting impact.”

Klick’s full list of MM+M Awards

  • GOLD: 867-5309 - The Cancer Support Community - Best Media Plan
  • GOLD: 867-5309 - The Cancer Support Community - Use of Customer Experience Marketing
  • GOLD: 867-5309 - The Cancer Support Community - Use of Hospital or Healthcare Services Marketing
  • GOLD: Inch by Inch (Project Inchstone) - Nestlé Compleat - Use of Film or Video

  • SILVER: 867-5309 - The Cancer Support Community - Point-of-Care Marketing
  • SILVER: 867-5309 - The Cancer Support Community - Use of Public Relations
  • SILVER: The Power of Choice: The Wayback Room - Incyte Dermatology - Health Equity and Social Awareness Campaign
  • SILVER: Miles to Miracle - Miracle Feet - Use of Social Media - Organic

About Klick Health

Klick Health is the world’s largest independent commercialization partner for life sciences companies. The agency helps life sciences brands achieve their full potential with best-in-class marketing strategy, media strategy and purchasing, medical affairs, medical publications and medical communications, value and market access services, real world evidence support, as well as technology and analytics consulting from clinical development through Loss of Exclusivity (LOE). Klick’s expertise is rooted in deep medical and scientific understanding and is powered by over 500 post-graduate, in-house medical experts; award-winning data science and AI capabilities; unrivaled decision sciences; and innovative, results-driven creative — all built on a foundation of proprietary technology platforms that have defined Klick since its founding.

One of the most-awarded advertising and medical affairs agencies on the planet, Klick has been recognized for its unique people-first culture and ranked a Best Managed Company, Great Place to Work, Best Workplace for Women, Best Workplace for Inclusion, Best Workplace for Professional Services, Most Admired Corporate Culture, and a FORTUNE Best Workplace in Advertising. This year, Klick made history when it was named Cannes Lions Healthcare Agency of the Year; Healthcare Network of the Year; and Independent Agency of the Year - Health. It was also recognized as Clio Health Independent Agency of the Year for the last four years, Campaign’s inaugural Global Healthcare & Pharma Agency of the Year (Gold), as well as London International Awards’ Global (and Regional) Independent Health & Pharma Agency of the Year. Similarly, Oxford PharmaGenesis is the only company in its sector to be named a three-time winner of the King’s (formerly Queen’s) Award for Enterprise. It also received a 2026 Longitude Prize on ALS and has been named Communique Awards’ Medical Affairs Agency of the Year; and PharmaTimes’ Medical Affairs Communications Team of the Year.

Established in 1997, Klick Health (including Oxford PharmaGenesis, Klick Katalyst, and btwelve) has offices in Toronto, Cambridge, Cardiff, London, Melbourne, New York, Oxford, Philadelphia, São Paulo, Saratoga Springs, and Singapore. data.title: AM Best Revises Outlooks to Positive for RAM Mutual Insurance Company
data.description:
AM Best Revises Outlooks to Positive for RAM Mutual Insurance Company

AM Best has revised the outlooks to positive from stable and affirmed the Financial Strength Rating of B++ (Good) and the Long-Term Issuer Credit Rating of “bbb+” (Good) of RAM Mutual Insurance Company (RAM) (Esko, MN).

The Credit Ratings (ratings) reflect RAM’s balance sheet strength, which AM Best assesses as very strong, as well as its marginal operating performance, limited business profile and appropriate enterprise risk management (ERM).

The outlook revisions to positive from stable reflect improved underwriting and overall operating results in each of the past two years and through the first half of 2026. The improvement in the company’s results was driven by significant rate increases and underwriting initiatives, such as mandatory deductibles and stricter underwriting guidelines following large losses between 2021 and 2023. AM Best expects the favorable trend in RAM’s operating performance to continue over the intermediate term, although results may remain subject to modest volatility from weather-related events.

RAM’s balance sheet strength is assessed as very strong, supported by the strongest levels of risk-adjusted capitalization, as measured by Best’s Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR). The very strong balance sheet assessment is supported further by favorable underwriting leverage metrics, strong liquidity and a conservative investment portfolio. The business profile assessment reflects RAM’s geographic concentration in Minnesota, which increases susceptibility to severe weather-related events. RAM’s ERM is assessed as appropriate, reflecting strong internal controls and an active and engaged board of directors that is involved in the risk management process.

This press release relates to Credit Ratings that have been published on AM Best’s website. For all rating information relating to the release and pertinent disclosures, including details of the office responsible for issuing each of the individual ratings referenced in this release, please see AM Best’s Recent Rating Activity web page. data.title: BIASC: SCAG'S SB 1087 "HOUSING KILLER" IS NOW LAW — SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA DESERVES MAJOR SCAG REFORM
data.description:
BIASC: SCAG'S SB 1087 "HOUSING KILLER" IS NOW LAW -- SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA DESERVES MAJOR SCAG REFORM

BIASC: SCAG'S SB 1087 "HOUSING KILLER" IS NOW LAW -- SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA DESERVES MAJOR SCAG REFORM

PR Newswire

IRVINE, Calif., Oct. 2, 2026

Building Industry says SCAG-backed legislation could increase housing costs, undermine local decision-making and raises serious questions about regional accountability.

IRVINE, Calif., Oct. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Building Industry Association of Southern California (BIASC) today expressed strong disappointment with the enactment of Senate Bill 1087 (Cabaldon), legislation sponsored and advanced by the Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG). Despite being designated as a "Housing Killer" bill by the statewide California Building Industry Association, the SCAG-sponsored bill was signed by Governor Gavin Newsom on Wednesday, September 30.

BIASC opposed the final version of the legislation because of concerns about housing affordability, local planning authority and the potential consequences of new regional transportation and land-use requirements.

The legislation comes as California continues to face a severe housing affordability and production challenge. BIASC believes SB 1087 will make that challenge more difficult by expanding the role of regional planning requirements tied to greenhouse-gas reduction and Vehicle Miles Traveled (VMT) targets.

"California cannot solve its housing affordability crisis by creating additional uncertainty around where and how housing can be built," said BIASC CEO Jeff Montejano. "SB 1087 may now be law, but the larger issue remains: Southern California deserves a regional planning system that is transparent, accountable to its member cities and counties, and aligned with the state's housing goals."

BIASC's September 28 letter opposing the bill pointed to research cited from UC Berkeley's Terner Center regarding the significant gap between California's existing housing plans and the state's Vehicle Miles Traveled reduction objectives. The letter argued that these competing policy mandates could have significant consequences for housing production and affordability. 

LEGAL AND HOUSING CONCERNS

Jennifer Hernandez, who leads West Coast Land Use & Environmental Law with Holland & Knight and advised the industry on California housing and environmental law, emphasized the broader legal implications of the legislation.

"Sustainable Communities Strategies are not simply planning exercises," Hernandez stated. "They operate within a statewide legal and policy framework that can affect housing production, transportation funding and litigation. California should not impose new regional mandates without fully evaluating their consistency with existing housing laws and their affordability consequences."

That language reflects the legal arguments presented in BIASC's letter, which states that Sustainable Communities Strategies operate within a statewide framework that can be litigated and used in decisions involving transportation and affordable-housing funding.

MORE THAN HALF A MILLION EMAILS

Members of the public, BIASC members and coalition partners generated 510,723 emails voicing concerns to elected officials about SB 1087 — the largest grassroots advocacy effort in BIASC history.

The opposition effort also generated:

  • Over 348,000 views of video demonstrating SB 1087 as a "Housing Killer" bill

  • Over 28,000 social media likes

  • Opposition from elected officials and regional stakeholders across Southern California

THE NEXT CHAPTER: SCAG REFORM

SB 1087's enactment does not end BIASC's involvement in regional policy.

BIASC will now focus on SCAG governance, transparency, accountability and the role of its 191 cities and six counties in major legislative and policy decisions.

"This is bigger than one bill," Montejano said. "The question now is how a regional organization representing millions of Southern Californians makes major policy decisions, how those decisions are communicated to its member agencies, and how elected representatives are given a meaningful voice in that process. Those are legitimate questions, and BIASC intends to pursue them."

BIASC will continue working with its members, local governments, elected officials and regional partners on reforms intended to strengthen transparency and accountability at SCAG.

About BIASC

The Building Industry Association of Southern California is the voice of the region's building industry, with five chapters offering localized services to building professionals from Ventura to the southern tip of Orange County.  For more than a century, the association has served its builder and associate members by anticipating, protecting, and promoting their common interests through a wide range of programs, services, councils, and committees. For more information on the Building Industry Association of Southern California, visit biasc.org. Follow BIASC on social media for the latest industry news: LinkedIn, Facebook and Instagram.

Contact:

Building Industry Association of Southern California (BIASC)
swidor@biasc.org

data.title: ICE Canada Midday: Canola Rising
data.description:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba--ICE Futures canola contracts were stronger at midday Friday, continuing their back-and-forth choppy trade of the past week.

November canola was up C$8.60 at C$820.40 per tonne at midsession, with chart-based positioning a feature as values held relatively rangebound.

Gains in Chicago soyoil accounted for some spillover buying interest in the Canadian oilseed, although soybeans were lower.

Seasonal harvest pressure tempered the advances, with warm and dry weather forecast across most of the Prairies over the next week.

Canadian farmers delivered 707,500 tonnes of canola into the commercial pipeline during the week ended Sept. 27, reported the Canadian Grain Commission. That was up 33% from the previous week.

Weekly canola exports of 130,700 tonnes were roughly triple what moved the previous week, bringing the crop-year-to-date total through eight weeks to 921,700 tonnes. That compares with 715,600 tonnes at the same point the previous year.

An estimated 61,400 canola contracts traded as of 11:47 a.m. ET.

data.title: BEYOND THE WALL A Collection of Rare Artwork Celebrating the Legacy of Pink Floyd For a Limited Time at Animazing Gallery in Las Vegas
data.description:
BEYOND THE WALL A Collection of Rare Artwork Celebrating the Legacy of Pink Floyd For a Limited Time at Animazing Gallery in Las Vegas

BEYOND THE WALL A Collection of Rare Artwork Celebrating the Legacy of Pink Floyd For a Limited Time at Animazing Gallery in Las Vegas

PR Newswire

LAS VEGAS, Oct. 2, 2026

LAS VEGAS, Oct. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Pink Floyd fans and art collectors alike will soon have a rare opportunity to get a peek "Beyond the Wall" in Las Vegas.

Animazing Gallery at Grand Canal Shoppes at The Venetian Resort Las Vegas announced plans today for a special exhibition and sale featuring an extraordinary collection of work celebrating the legacy of Pink Floyd. The show will run from October 16 through November 2 and will include work by acclaimed artist and sculptor Ginger Gilmour, the former wife of Pink Floyd guitarist David Gilmour; Gerald Scarfe, recognized for his work on The Wall and his long collaboration with the band and its members; Storm Thorgerson, who was responsible for many of the band's album covers including The Dark Side of the Moon, Meddle, Atom Heart Mother, and Wish You Were Here; and, many other featured artists.

Ginger Gilmour will be offering both original artwork and exclusive limited editions.

The show will also include an exclusive, signed limited edition print of Gerald Scarfe's Marching Hammers and The Scream featuring images from Pink Floyd's The Wall, as well as original production artwork from the animated film The Wall. He will also debut two new custom hand-painted guitars with artwork from The Wall that resulted from an exclusive arrangement between the artist and Animazing Gallery. The guitars were built in the famed Lynn Ellsworth custom shop and sent to Scarfe to hand paint for the show.

The exhibit will kick of with a private VIP collectors' event on Friday, October 16 from 6-9 p.m. The public opening is set for Saturday, October 17 from 4-7 p.m. Artists Ginger Gilmour, Mel Balatbat, Randy Martinez, Dale Benson, and Nancy Elhallak will be attending both events.

The full list of participating artists includes:

Ginger Gilmour

Gerald Scarfe

Storm Thorgerson

John Douglas

Mel Balatbat

Randy Martinez

Dale Benson

Nancy Elhallak

For more information about the "Beyond the Wall" exhibition and sale at Animazing Gallery, visit www.animazing.com or Instagram@animazinggallery, or call (702) 785-0061.

ABOUT GINGER GILMOUR

Ginger Gilmour, the former wife of Pink Floyd's guitarist David Gilmour, is an artist, sculptor, and visionary. On a perpetual quest for beauty, much of her work was inspired by Pink Floyd.

ABOUT GERALD SCARFE

Gerald Scarfe is an English satirical cartoonist and illustrator who also worked as a political cartoonist for The Sunday Times with his work appearing weekly. He is renowned for his lengthy collaboration with Pink Floyd, including creating the artwork for their 1982 "The Wall" album and its film adaptation and tour. He was also responsible for art for the band's "Welcome to the Machine" music video and much more. In 2010, he published The Making of Pink Floyd: The Wall, a book detailing his work with Pink Floyd and Roger Waters from 1974 to 2010.

ABOUT STORM THORGERSON

Storm Thorgerson is best known for his artwork that for four decades graced the covers of Pink Floyd albums. His more than four-decade relationship with members of the band goes back to his days attending school at Cambridge with Pink Floyd's founders Syd Barrett and Roger Waters.

For more information about the Beyond the Wall exhibit at Animazing Gallery, visit www.animazing.com or call (702) 785-0061.

ABOUT ANIMAZING GALLERY

Animazing Gallery began in 1984 as a gallery specializing in conceptual animation art. Over time, the collection expanded to include works by a wide range of renowned illustrators and pop culture artists. Animazing Gallery has become an industry stronghold for illustration art and contemporary art inspired by the masters of illustration.

Nicholas Leone, owner of Animazing Gallery, serves as a consultant for numerous auction houses and handles gallery sales and acquisitions. He curates and hosts pop up events throughout the United States to celebrate gallery artists and their works. The company has two galleries located in Grand Canal Shoppes at The Venetian Resort in Las Vegas featuring an abundant repertoire of work by classic illustrators and contemporary artists. 

ABOUT GRAND CANAL SHOPPES

Located inside The Venetian Resort Las Vegas, the center boasts 160 specialty brands and world-class restaurants nestled around a charming and faithful reproduction of Venice's Grand Canal, complete with cobbled walkways, street-side cafes, and live entertainment. Signature brands including Burberry, Jimmy Choo, Michael Kors, Louis Vuitton, and Tory Burch create an unparalleled retail environment that includes a star-studded line-up of restaurants headed by famous celebrity chefs: Wolfgang Puck's CUT, Emeril Lagasse's Delmonico Steakhouse, Buddy Valastro's Buddy V's and Carlo's Bakery, Lorena Garcia's CHICA, as well as Mercato della Pescheria, SUGARCANE, SUSHISAMBA, and Smith & Wollensky. The center is also home to ATOMIC SALOON SHOW by Spiegelworld. For more information, visit www.grandcanalshoppes.com.

Capital Bancorp Investor Alert: Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC Investigates Adequacy of Price and Process in Proposed Sale of Capital Bancorp, Inc. - CBNK

Former Attorney General of Louisiana Charles C. Foti, Jr., Esq. and the law firm of Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC (“KSF”) are investigating the proposed sale of Capital Bancorp, Inc. ("Capital") (NasdaqGS: CBNK) to Peoples Bancorp Inc. ("Peoples") (NasdaqGS: PEBO). Under the terms of the proposed transaction, shareholders of Capital will receive 1.11 shares of Peoples common stock for each share of Capital that they own. Upon closing of the proposed transaction, Capital shareholders are expected to own approximately 32% of the combined company. KSF is seeking to determine whether this consideration and the process that led to it are adequate, or whether the consideration undervalues the Company.

data.description:
1004 GMT - Glencore could beat its new marketing unit forecast this year given the current environment, RBC analyst Ben Davis writes. He cites volatility, supply chain disruption and refining margins. The miner and commodity trader raised its guidance for marketing adjusted EBIT this year to over $5 billion compared with previous guidance of around $4.9 billion. It also raised its longer-term guidance for the metric to between $2.8 billion and $4.2 billion from $2.3 billion to $3.5 billion. RBC estimates 2026 marketing EBIT of $5.4 billion compared with consensus of $5.18 billion. Davis adds that the more important driver for the stock is the multiple attached to a trading business. RBC has an outperform rating on the stock and 660 pence target price. Shares are up 1.7% at 554.50 pence, and 38% higher over the year-to-date. (ian.walker@wsj.com)

--

Natural Gas Moves Lower as EIA Reports Record-High Production -- Market Talk

1003 ET - Natural gas is down 0.3%, retreating under the $3 per-mmBtu mark after the EIA reported that in July, U.S. natural gas production reached a record high. The agency says that July production landed at 137 billion cubic feet a day, continuing the gradual and stable run-up in natural gas production seen since 2010. This new record replaces the record set after 5 months of new record-highs in 2025, says the EIA. Mild weather has been a factor pressing on natural gas futures today, with electrical power demand seen as limited. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)

--

Crude Oil Falls To Close Out the Week -- Market Talk

0947 ET - Crude oil futures are sliding as more barrels of oil move through the Strait of Hormuz, although the risk of new military incursions remains strong. "The underlying picture remains fragmented," says Ole Hansen of Saxo Bank in a note. On the one hand, Saudi Arabian crude oil exports picked up in late September, but on the other is the present threat of further U.S. strikes on Middle Eastern infrastructure. "The U.S. decision to send another carrier group towards the region underlines why improving flows have yet to remove the market's risk premium," says Hansen. WTI crude is down 4% to $89.22 a barrel, while Brent crude falls 2.7% to $99.56 a barrel. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)

--

Gold Climbs on U.S. Jobs Report Miss -- Market Talk

0905 ET - Gold futures jumped following the release of the September Non-Farm Payrolls report and the latest unemployment figures by the Labor Department - with the number of jobs added coming in well below analyst expectations. The miss has Treasury yields and the U.S. dollar lower, in turn buoying other assets like gold. It's part of a repricing of inflation risk, says Artem Bakushev of Monaxa in a note. "The Fed focused on yesterday's inflation problem, while today's labour data is showing the cost of staying too tight for too long," says Bakushev. Most-active gold is up 1.1% to $4,248 a troy ounce. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)

--

Oil Falls 1% Despite Middle East Escalation Fears -- Market Talk

0740 GMT - Oil prices ease on signs that Gulf crude exports are recovering, although tensions in the region remain elevated amid concerns over further military action and attacks on shipping. In early European trading, front-month Brent crude for December is down 1% at $101.26 a barrel, while WTI futures slide 1.8% to $91.24 a barrel. According to The Wall Street Journal, the Pentagon is sending a third aircraft-carrier strike group and additional Marine Corps ships to the Middle East as President Trump considers renewing strikes on Iran after the midterm elections. Meanwhile, physical prices remain elevated as the market worries the U.S. might soon impose a ban on diesel exports. "Tight distillate markets, reduced refined-product availability and uncertainty around Middle East shipping continue to support prices, but any evidence of stronger supply flows can quickly trigger profit-taking," says Naeem Aslam from Zaye Capital Markets. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)

--

BHP's New Bull More Upbeat on Copper -- Market Talk

0638 GMT - BofA Securities turns bullish on BHP, citing an improved outlook for copper prices. It raises its share-price target on BHP to 68 Australian dollars from A$65 and upgrades the stock to buy from neutral. That follows a 20% lift in its long-term copper price forecast to US$13,577/metric ton. BofA views a site visit to BHP's Australian copper operations in November as a key catalyst. "We expect the site visit to give the market greater confidence in the ramp-up of mined volumes," it says. Shares ended up 1.6% at A$61.21. (rhiannon.hoyle@wsj.com; @RhiannonHoyle)

--

Lynas Deal For Meteoric to Help With Heavy Rare Earths Expansion -- Market Talk

0453 GMT - Lynas's planned acquisition of Meteoric Resources appears to be at least initially about securing heavy rare-earths supply for its expanding Malaysia refining plant, says UBS. The bank says the deal demonstrates the increased interest in Brazil for rare earths. It says it's "mindful the potential (risk and/or opportunity) for further LYC investment in the region, particularly around refining capacity." UBS trims its share-price target on Lynas to A$21.00 from A$22.50. That reflects the deal and capex required to develop Meteoric's Caldeira project, it says. The bank keeps a buy rating. Shares in Lynas are up 0.6% at A$12.72, after falling by 8.6% Thursday on the takeover news. (rhiannon.hoyle@wsj.com; @RhiannonHoyle)

--

Palm Oil Falls, Weighed by Lower Soybean Oil Prices -- Market Talk

0302 GMT - Palm oil falls in Asian trading, tracking overnight declines in soybean oil on the Chicago Board of Trade. Technical analysis suggests the outlook for crude palm oil futures remains bearish, AmInvestment Bank says in a note. However, global vegetable oil prices could rise in the coming months due to tighter supply as disruptions to Black Sea sunflower oil shipments coincide with declining South American soyoil exports, it adds. AmInvestment Bank sees resistance at 4,611 ringgit a ton and support at 4,512 ringgit a ton. The Bursa Malaysia Derivatives contract for December delivery is down 36 ringgit at 4,518 ringgit a ton. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)

--

Copper Flat as Tight Supply Offset by Stronger Dollar -- Market Talk

0157 GMT - Copper prices are flat in early Asian trade. Although tight supply and resilient demand continue to support prices, a stronger dollar and higher U.S. Treasury yields are limiting the upside. Copper concentrate supply remains tight, putting pressure on smelters' margins, and tighter domestic scrap availability has helped keep refined-copper inventories low, Minmetals Futures analysts say in a note. The U.S.-London copper spread also remains elevated on expectations of potential U.S. tariffs on refined copper, they add. The three-month LME copper contract is flat at $14,243.00 a ton.(jiahui.huang@wsj.com; @ivy_jiahuihuang)

--

Gold Falls; U.S. Dollar, Yields Key Obstacles for Price Gain -- Market Talk

0054 GMT - Gold falls in early Asian trade. The dollar and Treasury yields are currently the main obstacles to gold returning to its broader bullish path, says Simon-Peter Massabni, head of business development at XS.com. Moderating inflation creates an opportunity for gold, but economic resilience and elevated yields are preventing a decisive breakout, Massabni adds. "The real turning point will not come from a single day of price action, but from markets sustainably repricing the path of U.S. monetary policy," Massabni says. Spot gold is 0.4% lower at $4,160.68 a troy ounce, taking weekly losses to nearly 3%. (kimberley.kao@wsj.com)

--

Rio Tinto Best Bet for Those Constructive Iron Ore, Cautious Copper, Bull Says -- Market Talk

0001 GMT - Rio Tinto is the cleanest way to be long iron ore and cautious on copper while keeping exposure to growth in the base metal, Macquarie says. It upgrades the stock to outperform from neutral. "Rio is still iron-ore anchored (circa 50% of segment earnings for CY27), so it captures our view on a near-term recovery in the commodity, but it also has genuine, growing copper exposure," says the bank. Copper accounted for roughly 27% of group Ebitda in 2025, and could rise to about 36% by the end of the decade, it says. "Critically, it [Rio] has lagged BHP by circa 20% year to date, so investors buy iron ore leverage plus copper growth without paying BHP's copper 'tourist' premium," Macquarie says. It keeps a neutral rating on BHP. (rhiannon.hoyle@wsj.com; @RhiannonHoyle)

data.title: Golden Gate Global Announces USCIS Approval of The Mammoth Collection, Its 17th Approved EB-5 Project in California
data.description:
Golden Gate Global Announces USCIS Approval of The Mammoth Collection, Its 17th Approved EB-5 Project in California

Golden Gate Global is pleased to announce that The Mammoth Collection, a rural EB-5 project in California’s Greater Mammoth region, has received project approval from U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), further extending Golden Gate Global’s 100% USCIS project approval rate.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261002647684/en/

The Mammoth Collection is Golden Gate Global’s 17th EB-5 project in the State of California. The fully funded project financed the development of a 101-key Residence Inn by Marriott and an 80-key Hampton Inn by Hilton and was structured for 45 EB-5 investors. The investment features a senior secured loan, a first deed of trust across both hotel assets, and a developer completion guarantee.

The approval comes on the heels of USCIS approval of Anasu Resort Phase 2, another rural EB-5 project sponsored by Golden Gate Global in California Wine Country across Lake and Napa counties. Anasu is the vision of hospitality pioneer Adrian Zecha, founder of Aman Resorts and co-founder of Regent International Hotels.

Golden Gate Global’s California portfolio has also recently received recognition beyond the EB-5 industry. Appellation Healdsburg, a Golden Gate Global-sponsored project in Sonoma County, was recently named the Best Resort in California by Travel + Leisure magazine.

Since 2011, Golden Gate Global has focused on bringing institutional-quality investments to the immigrant investor community. The firm believes strongly in the depth and resilience of California’s economy, from Silicon Valley and Hollywood to Wine Country, hospitality, tourism, and real estate. With 17 sponsored EB-5 projects in the state, Golden Gate Global has established itself as the largest sponsor of EB-5 projects in California.

The project approvals also come at an important time for investors considering the EB-5 Green Card program. USCIS filing fees for Form I-526E are scheduled to increase significantly beginning November 30, 2026. In addition, the minimum EB-5 investment amount is expected to increase beginning January 1, 2027 for qualifying Targeted Employment Area projects from $800,000 today to more than $900,000, as part of the program’s scheduled inflation adjustment.

For prospective investors considering the EB-5 Green Card program, these recent approvals reflect Golden Gate Global’s continued commitment to sponsoring institutional-quality EB-5 projects in California. With a growing portfolio across the state and a 100% USCIS project approval rate, the firm remains focused on combining strong project fundamentals with experienced sponsorship and disciplined execution.

Jane Baklashov
info@3gfund.com
